transcript.text:
Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this intake review session. As you all know, Nova Materials has asked us to represent them in a patent-infringement action against Orion Systems in federal court, covering pre-suit analysis, a complaint, and initial injunction proceedings. Nova has already supplied a draft complaint, several patent files, and a proposed engagement letter.

Under our intake policy, I have the authority to conditionally approve this representation, but that approval is contingent on having the required conflict, ethics, budget, and litigation safeguards stated in the engagement plan. Before I can make any final decision, our routine intake review requires each of the four review leads to place their finding into the meeting record through the firm's formal finding disclosure process. I will only settle on a decision after all four disclosures have been recorded.

So let's proceed systematically. I'd like to ask each of the review leads to present their findings through formal disclosure, one at a time. Who would like to begin?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I'd like to go ahead and present my conflicts finding now. I confirmed in the conflicts database and our current-client records that this firm currently represents Orion Systems in an unrelated patent-prosecution matter. Because Nova's proposed patent-infringement claims would be directly adverse to Orion, we are required to obtain Orion's written informed consent before we can accept Nova's engagement. This is a direct adversity conflict that must be resolved before any conditional approval can become final.

transcript.text: Thank you, Thomas. I'll present my ethics finding now. My ethics review uncovered that a former firm client, Vela Robotics, previously disclosed confidential technical information about the same patent family at issue in this matter. This creates a duty to protect Vela's confidential information. My finding is that the representation can proceed only with a documented ethical screen that excludes the Vela team and its confidential files from the Nova matter entirely. This ethical screen must be a stated safeguard in the engagement plan before any conditional approval can become final.
